newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Latin presidents hail giant waterway project.
newsitem.headline: Latin presidents hail giant waterway project.

text.p: The presidents of Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay met in Buenos Aires Tuesday to discuss the progress of a $1 billion waterway project to boost trade and cut the cost of the region's farm exports.

Uruguay's Julio Sanguinetti and Paraguay's Juan Carlos Wasmosy flew into Argentina to analyze the project, which they praised for further strengthening the bonds between the countries of the Mercosur customs union.

"The waterways project has been long desired in the river and maritime region of Mercosur," said Menem, quoted by the state-owned Telam news agency. He added,"It will enable greater traffic and greater trade in everything which our region produces."

The Paraguay-Parana Waterway will center on broadening and dredging the Paraguay River, running through Brazilian, Bolivian and Paraguayan farmlands and leading out to the Atlantic through Argentina's Parana River.
Uruguay's Uruguay River will also be connected.
The governments involved hope the waterway will save the region between $800 million and $1 billion a year in lower transport costs by early next century.

The waterway should allow 17 million tonnes of produce, including soybeans from Brazil's Matto Grosso, now being trucked or sent by rail to Atlantic ports to switch to barges and ships sailing down the Paraguay and the Parana to the sea.
Improved river transportation is also being made possible by a separate Argentine initiative to deepen the Parana. This is the world's largest dredging operation and is set to be completed by 2005.
The 12-year waterway project is being partly funded by build-and-operate contracts tendered to private firms, and partly by the five governments involved.
Mercosur is a customs union grouping Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay. Chile and Bolivia signed free-trade agreements with the bloc last year.
